name: The Hinterlands
summary: The Hinterlands still bear the Amani's old claims, while Wildhammer dwarves hold Aerie Peak. Forest trolls keep their ruined temples, and the Revantusk have made a village on the eastern coast.

sections.title: A Land of Clashing Claims
sections.body:
The Amani forest trolls ruled the Hinterlands long before humans or dwarves came to northern Lordaeron. Their defeat in the ancient Troll Wars broke the empire into separate tribes. Centuries later, the War of the Three Hammers drove the Wildhammer dwarves from Grim Batol.

They migrated north and settled above ground at Aerie Peak. There, they tamed native gryphons and kept their shamanic traditions as they built a great stronghold in the heights. The forest trolls saw them as squatters on ancestral land. Skirmishes and raids have kept the feud alive ever since.

sections.title: Tribes of the Forest
sections.body:
Three forest troll tribes occupy the dense woods and ruined temples. The strongest are the brutal Vilebranch, who hold the terraced temple city of Jintha'Alor and the towering Altar of Zul. Farther south, the weaker Witherbark cling to Shadra'Alor and Hiri'Watha.

The nomadic Revantusk were long scorned by their cousins and had no true home. After the Third War, they made a treaty with Thrall's New Horde. With aid from orcs and Forsaken, they founded Revantusk Village on the eastern sea cliffs and claimed a coastal stronghold of their own.

sections.title: The Slumbering Rift
sections.body: Seradane, the great tree in the northern Hinterlands, shelters a portal to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons and creatures of nature guard the grove. Now the Emerald Nightmare seeps across the portal's threshold, twisting once-benevolent drakes and dragonspawn into furious guardians.

faq.q: How do I get to the Hinterlands?
faq.answer: Travelers from either faction enter the Hinterlands from Hillsbrad Foothills. They go northeast through a mountain pass beyond Durnholde Keep. Alliance travelers follow the road to Aerie Peak, while Horde travelers cross east through the wilderness to Revantusk Village on the coast.
Falstad Wildhammer, Lord of Aerie Peak, leads the Wildhammer clan there. Thane Kurdran Wildhammer led the clan during the Second War.

faq.q: Why are the Revantusk trolls allied with the Horde?
faq.answer: The nomadic Revantusk sought protection and an end to wandering. The hostile Vilebranch and Witherbark rejected Horde emissaries. The New Horde gave the Revantusk resources and soldiers to build Revantusk Village on the coast, earning their loyalty against local rivals.

Jintha'Alor is an ancient fortress cut into the southern cliffs in many tiers. It is the chief stronghold of the ruthless Vilebranch, with sacrificial altars and elite warriors. Its witch doctors perform blood rites for their dark loas.

faq.q: What is the Great Tree at Seradane?
faq.answer: Seradane, one of Azeroth's Great Trees, shelters a portal to the Emerald Dream. Green dragons and wildkin watch over the grove.

Quel'Danil Lodge is a forest retreat kept by Highvale high elves. The Scourge spared it from a direct assault on Quel'Thalas. Its rangers and scholars work with nearby Wildhammer dwarves, sharing intelligence about hostile forest trolls.

angles.text: As a Wildhammer or visiting Bronzebeard, you find dwarven life at Aerie Peak beneath open skies. Shamanic power and legendary gryphons shape life there.
In the Hinterlands, ancient Amani glory lives on as bloodlines clash over temple steps. The Revantusk show that forest trolls still have a place in the New Horde.
The Wildhammer dwarves prize their fierce independence. Aid their outposts and the high elves of Quel'Danil to build goodwill against shared troll threats.
Revantusk Village gives the Horde an eastern beachhead in northern Lordaeron. To hold it, you must beat back the fierce Vilebranch.
Seradane's ancient tree is closely tied to the Emerald Dream. Watch carefully for the creeping rot of the Nightmare.
